name: Draft Reward Screen
description: The choose-one-of-three that builds the deck. After a combat clears, this component offers a small set of cards drawn from inventory.loot_table pools, and the chosen card enters the run deck through inventory.deck_manager — the screen never edits piles itself, because deck membership is the deck manager's bookkeeping, not a UI concern. The skip option is first-class: thinning is a strategy, and a draft with no skip forces bloat on players who already know better. This component owns the offer and the choice. It does not own the pools (inventory.loot_table does, as content) or the rarity math behind them, and it does not own drafts that happen outside combat rewards — progression.draft_on_level_up is the sibling for level-up choices, kept separate because combat drafts grow the deck while level-up drafts grow the build.

inputs.name: choicesOffered
inputs.description: Cards shown per draft. Three is the genre standard: two feels like a coin flip, four reads as a wall.

inputs.name: allowSkip
inputs.description: Whether the player may take nothing. Keep it true unless the design specifically wants forced bloat as pressure.

inputs.name: skipReward
inputs.description: Optional compensation for skipping (heal, currency). Null means skipping is its own reward: a thinner deck.

outputs.name: lastOffer
outputs.description: The card ids most recently presented, kept for UI restore after interruption.

outputs.name: draftsSkipped
outputs.description: How often the player took nothing — the clearest signal that draft pools are mis-tuned.
